misconceptions.description: Treating a design rationale such as 'it should feel easier' as if it were already a testable usability hypothesis
misconceptions.trigger: learner submits a prediction using subjective adjectives (easier, intuitive, cleaner) with no observable outcome
misconceptions.feedback: A rationale explains why you changed the design; a hypothesis predicts an observable behavior. Convert the adjective into something a moderator could count.

misconceptions.description: Stating a prediction with no direction or numeric threshold against a baseline
misconceptions.trigger: learner predicts an outcome will 'improve' or 'be better' without a baseline or target
misconceptions.feedback: Add a direction and a threshold against a stated baseline (for example, 8 of 10 versus a 4 of 10 baseline) so the session can confirm or disconfirm it.

misconceptions.description: Writing a hypothesis with no condition under which it could fail, so every observation is read as confirmation
misconceptions.trigger: learner reports a prediction confirmed when no result could have disconfirmed it
misconceptions.feedback: State the failure condition explicitly. If no observed outcome could have disproven the prediction, it is not yet a testable hypothesis.
